subject: ancientTreant
pitch:
Category: Fantastical creature.
Subject: ancient treant, walking tree guardian.
Style: Blizzard/Warcraft.
reasoning:
I'm picturing a Warcraft-style treant—chunky bark, glowing eyes, mossy canopy, root legs, branch arms—and planning how to build it using the available geometry API like joints, sweeps, and surfaces.

Now I'm working out the skeleton structure: hips, spine chain up through chest and neck, a head joint, and shoulder-to-hand arm chains, along with a bark paint function that layers dark grain with mossy mottling. I'm figuring out joint placement and parenting for the torso and head so the proportions read correctly at roughly 4.5 meters tall.

Adding leg sweeps...

Computing foot pad geometry as a flattened ellipsoid so the bottom sits at zero, then moving to arms—setting shoulder and hand target positions, checking segment lengths add up to the needed reach, and figuring out which direction the elbow should bend outward.

Now I'm planning hands: fingers as small chains of two joints each using the "digit" role, three fingers plus a thumb per hand, catmull/bezier paths fanning out from the wrist base point.

The wrist joint becomes the parent for fingers and palm, with the palm formed by a scaled sphere at the wrist. For the head, I'm placing a gnarled box-shaped skull joint with a separate jaw joint below it, adding a brow ridge and tusk-like jaw details to give it a monstrous silhouette.

Eyes get glowing amber plane textures with dark sockets behind them, a nose formed from a forward-pointing cone nub, and moss-like beard cards hanging from the jaw, with a dark interior box standing in for the mouth. I'm aligning the head center above the torso's tapered chest so the proportions read correctly from hips to shoulders.

Adding a head joint parented to the spine with aim toward the front, plus a short neck joint between spine and head. Now I'm planning the canopy — a crown of leaf cards and foliage blobs above the head and shoulders, with antler-like branches radiating from the top of the head using bezier curves.

Building leaf clusters...

Now I'm adding bark surface details—scattered plate ridges, knot rings, and a glowing rune decal placed on the chest—plus a skirt of draping roots encircling the hips.

Writing bark and leaf paint functions...

Now I'm designing the glowing amber eye SVG with an almond-shaped socket, slit pupil, and angled brow for an angry expression, placed on a mirrored plane using tilt parameters to achieve the asymmetric slant.

Working through the viewer-perspective math, I conclude svg u-right maps to model +X, so for an eye at x>0 the inner corner sits toward smaller x (svg left) and should be drawn low there, while x<0 eyes mirror that. I'm defining an eyeTex function taking an innerLeft flag, then moving on to build a glowing cyan-green rune texture for a chest decal with strong glow.

Now I'm importing a glow helper for the eyes, designing a leaf-shaped SVG texture with a vein, and planning moss-strand beard cards hung from frame points along the jaw across the chin. I'm also sketching out antler/branch crown geometry using a bezier-sweep twig function with mini branches and leaf clusters at the tips, then turning to the arms.

Now I'm adding mossy vine cards on the forearms, bark-blob shoulder knobs built from scaled dodecahedrons on a spine bone with foliage on top, and defining the torso's spine chain as a catmull-rom path with three named segments, shaping its width over the length with a smoothstep-based radius function for a wider chest.

I'm sizing the neck and shoulder radii so arms sprout naturally from the shoulder knobs, rounding the top sweep cap to overlap into the head, adding a scaled icosahedron pelvis blob at the hips as a bark bone joint, and setting up tapering thigh radii for the leg sweep.

Now I'm defining the leg sweep radii through three keyframes, placing a dodecahedron knee knob at the joint, setting the hips as the root bone that legs parent from, and configuring the limb bend direction so knees flex forward.

For the feet, I'm placing the ankle target height, attaching an ellipsoid foot bone, then sweeping bezier curves for three forward toes plus a heel, each with tapered radii, keeping them as simple sweeps off the ankle rather than full chains since the digits are kept separate.

I'm skipping lathe-based knotholes and firefly effects, instead scattering small cone-shaped bark ridges across the torso using a dark flat color, filtered to avoid the underside, and embedding them into the trunk surface sweep.

Now I'm adding bracket fungus shapes—flattened cylinders in orange and cream tones—scattered along the torso and leg sides, keeping the part count reasonable around 150 total. For the head, I'm sketching brow ridges as small rotated boxes positioned above the face, angling them inward to give the face a fiercer, angrier expression.

Adding more head details...

Checking the eye sockets sit flush against the face front, adding a dark recessed box for depth, then placing brow ridges and moss/vine details across the back and crown of the head using small twig segments radiating outward.

Adding leaf card scatter to the blob surfaces with slight lean and flow direction, then placing shoulder and upper back foliage clusters on the spine bones. I'm sketching out elbow, hand, and wrist details and planning vine cards hanging from forearm sweep frames with a moss texture.

Now I'm settling on a texture set—eyes, runes, leaf, moss, maybe fungus spots—and deciding to add a glowing rune decal on the chest plus small ones on the shoulders, using a surface raycast to place the chest decal accurately.

Setting up the skeleton structure next: defining helper functions for leaf blobs, wiring bone joints for the arms and hands, and building out the spine-to-neck-to-head joint chain with proper parent references and aim directions.

Still working out finger positions...

Now I'm planning the mushroom colors, moss strand SVG shapes, and root skirt geometry using angular placement around the base.
